Identity audit removed a same-name static-data leak for Romero. Romero is making his UFC debut on three days' notice at featherweight. Zero-UFC opponent evidence caps McGhee despite the raw probability.
All three method layers favor Pinas KO strongly, but the winner probability is below the 60% method gate. Side remains modest despite Pinas' recent knockout form.
Rodriguez has only one official UFC bout while Coria has three and remains unbeaten in the UFC. Sparse-sample uncertainty trims the displayed confidence without flipping the model side.

Five UFC bouts versus an experienced opponent gives this substantially better evidence density than the debutant-heavy favorites. Baseline, calibrated and residual method layers all favor KO; calibrated conditional KO is 74.2% and exact joint KO mass is 61.3%.
Soldic's elite KSW history is real but sits outside the UFC-stat winner model, and this is his UFC debut after a 590-day MMA layoff. Keep the model side but treat it as low-confidence.
Low-margin model side. Ribovics missed lightweight by 0.5 lb; the bout continues at catchweight. Weight miss lowers confidence but does not justify a directional flip.

Silva's 8-0 UFC run and model edge remain intact, but Wang brings elite striking efficiency. First UFC five-round assignment for both plus Salt Lake City altitude widens uncertainty; method gate does not clear.
Talbott has the age/size/current-form advantages, while Figueiredo's experience and grappling keep upset risk meaningful. Talbott's roughly 10-month layoff prevents a higher confidence tier.
